Tamper-evidence, not enforcement. README.md is the never-author-status sentence, the gate approve row, and the skillTextLines cell. examples/ unchanged.

T-001.Title: Record per-Decision fingerprint and write draft to approved

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: AC-HEAD-RED (fingerprint-attr): before any production edit, in its own tool round trip, add a bun test in src/gates/core.test.ts. A permitting recorded approve of a draft spec writes a Decision whose attributes include fingerprint (SHA-256 lowercase hex of the on-disk spec.xml bytes after the status write) and artifact with value spec. Those are attributes, never children. A non-Requirement child still makes parseDecisionNode return invalid. A historical Decision without those attributes still lists as valid. Refuse and apply Decisions do not carry fingerprint or artifact. Do not assert per-Decision distinctness or the surgical status write in this case. HEAD today: GateDecisionRecord has no such fields (src/gates/ledger.ts:109-114). Record fail, signature kind test key fingerprint-attr. Run only this case. Do not land the writer in this round trip.

AC-HEAD-RED (per-decision): before the same production edit, in its own tool round trip, add a bun test in src/gates/core.test.ts. Two permitting approve writes in one bundle, first targeting spec then plan via default target order, produce two Decisions. The second stores its own fingerprint of plan.xml and does not copy the first fingerprint. baseCommit on the second still copies the first stored value when one exists. The Decision list only grows. The pair is distinguishable by artifact and fingerprint. Do not assert child-element invalidity in this case. HEAD today: the second Decision is often byte-identical to the first (F95). Record fail, signature kind test key per-decision. Run only this case.

AC-HEAD-RED (status-write): before the same production edit, in its own tool round trip, add a bun test in src/gates/core.test.ts. A permitting recorded approve whose target root status is draft writes approved onto that root attribute and does not re-serialize the rest of the file through serializeGraceXmlDocument (byte identity except that attribute). A target already approved is not rewritten before hashing. apply and archive recorded permits do not write status. argv token record false writes no status (isolation pin in this case's siblings, not a second recorded red; HEAD already holds it). Do not assert fingerprint attribute shape in this case. HEAD today: runGate never touches spec.xml or plan.xml (src/gates/command.ts:89-108). Record fail, signature kind test key status-write. Run only this case.

Production then pins then pass (F84): in the approve command record path, never inside evaluateApproveGate, select the target (spec whose status is not approved; else plan.xml present whose status is not approved; else plan.xml present; else spec), surgically replace only the root status attribute when it is draft, hash whole file bytes with SHA-256 lowercase hex (import digestProjectFile or duplicate that one-liner; do not edit src/grace-cursor.ts), and record fingerprint and artifact on that Decision. recordGateDecision never copies an earlier fingerprint. Parse copies the new attributes when present, including forced and reason so T-002 can fill them. Omit forced when unused. Descriptions no longer say approve never authors status; apply, archive, and verdict still do not write status. GATE_SUBCOMMANDS is unchanged. Then record pass.

T-002.Title: Forced permit hatch and approve command argv

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: AC-HEAD-RED (force-hatch): before adding argv tokens force, reason, and artifact, in its own tool round trip, add a bun test in src/gates/core.test.ts. Unresolved IC-* clarification, argv token force with a non-empty argv token reason: records a permit with forced true and that reason, writes status, and fingerprints. Requirement children still show the failed check. Force with empty or missing reason writes nothing and exits non-zero. A permit without force omits the forced attribute. Boolean space form for force is refused the same way argv token record space form is. Terminal statuses (applied, superseded, cancelled, rejected) refuse the status write even under force. Sibling it()s for those guards are the same property, not extra recorded reds. Optional argv token artifact with values spec or plan overrides default targeting (bounding, not a second red). HEAD today: no force argv exists on approve. Record fail, signature kind test key force-hatch. Run only this case. Do not land the hatch in this round trip.

Production then pins then pass (F84): force is command-path. When argv token force is true and argv token reason is non-empty, a clarification refuse is recorded as a permit with forced true and the supplied reason; status is written; bytes are fingerprinted. evaluateApproveGate stays clarification-only and git-free (AC-EVALUATE-UNCHANGED; stay-true; do not record a fail). gate apply still does not write status and still does not refuse on a missing or mismatched fingerprint (AC-APPLY-UNCHANGED; stay-true; do not record a fail). Split approve args from the shared factory as needed so force, reason, and artifact live on approve only. Update src/query/command.test.ts boolean-site exact pins (sites.length is 25 at HEAD; adding force as boolean moves that count; F33: re-measure, do not freeze the post-change number in this plan). Then record pass.
